title: C05 Beast Feast
body:
_When a small village’s monster defense system fails, the local heroes must venture into the endless caverns below to fix it—and cook up trouble for the creatures that stand in their way!_

### Campaign Frame

#### The Pitch
The rustic, peaceful village of Elmore sits atop the Plover Caves, a labyrinthine system of caverns full of dangerous and delectable creatures. When the powerful magic keeping the villagers safe begins to fail, the bravest among them must descend into the caves to save the day. In a Beast Feast campaign, you’ll play everyday heroes diving into the Plover Caves to reignite the magic lure that lies in its depths — and cook up delicious meals. Welcome to a culinary world of zoophagous delight, where the beasts you fight become the food you eat!

#### Tone & Feel
- Absurd, Comedic, Creepy, Fun, Lighthearted, Silly

#### Themes
- Circle of Life
- Friendship & Loyalty
- Nature’s Bounty, Overcoming Fear
- Violence & Peace

#### Touchstones
_Delicious in Dungeon, Monster Hunter World, One Piece_

#### Overview
Long ago, within the heart of the **Plover Caves**, **Hylaeus the Forest Mage** (she/her) cast a powerful spell, creating a Lure that draws dangerous creatures from the surrounding area into the caverns. For centuries, this kept any harm from coming to the village of **Elmore**. However, the caves are now filled to the brim with strange, unexpected creatures from across the region—and the remnants of outsiders brave or foolhardy enough to venture into them. But nobody from Elmore is foolish enough to be caught dead in the caves. The quiet, rustic village is full of bakers and weavers, farmers and cobblers, with ne’er a sword in sight. The villagers are more concerned about not mucking up their contribution to the yearly Stewpot Festival than the dangers outside their walls.

That was until the village’s beloved halfling mayor **Doug Dougle** (he/him) was attacked by a dangerous creature during his daily hike through Plover Woods. The Lure created by Hylaeus all those years ago is fading, and with it, Elmore’s protection. As increasingly dangerous beasts stalk the woods, the villagers have banded together to reignite the ancient spell, calling on anyone who might pick up a blade to descend into the caves and save their people. Unfortunately, the defenseless people of Elmore have ceased hunting and foraging in Plover Woods for fear of attack until the Lure is reactivated—there isn’t much to spare, so every bite in town is precious. Anyone venturing into the caves will have to hunt and prepare their own food while they’re down there!

The easiest way to find the Plover Caves is to take the western road out of Elmore and follow the birdsong of piping plovers. Old tales from this area say these small birds are the only creatures that move freely in and out of the tunnels without losing themselves to the depths, so following them almost always leads to an entrance—or an exit.

The old tales also say the Plover Caves are endless—this isn’t true, but it might as well be. They stretch on for hundreds of miles underground, deeper and more sprawling than even the most adventurous explorer could map in their lifetime. The entry path leads down on a sharp decline for miles until it finally splits into many branches leading to various regions within the cave system. Here, different biomes are home to unique creatures, wonderous flora, and valuable treasures left behind by adventurers past. The deeper you go, the more dangerous and delicious the creatures are, and the more precious and powerful the treasure is. And even deeper still lies the Lure.

Those from Elmore might be surprised to find there are many people happily living and working in the dark, dangerous caverns. Most reside in camps, but more permanent residents have small cabins carved out of rock along the tunnels. The culture in the Plover Caves is very communal, and ambitious folks have set up shops for bartering or trade. Most major caverns even host a Berry’s—the chain of small restaurants that serve the catch of the day, fresh and hot, in exchange for gold. Residents might stop in when they’re too tired or ingredient-poor to cook for themselves, but Berry’s restaurants are also hubs for gossip, entertainment, and warnings about what dangerous beasts might be lurking nearby.

### Player Characters

- 

### Outline

After the attack on Mayor Dougle, the local alchemist, Carat (they/them), approaches the party. Worried for the safety of the town, they ask the party to delve into the Plover Caves to locate a particular ingredient — ghost scorpion venom. Carat can transmute twelve drops of this venom into a spicy paste, which they can spread around the borders of the village to temporarily keep dangerous creatures at bay.

Carat explains that ghost scorpions tend to make their nests by flattening the tall grasses of the Overgrowth into strange circular patterns. To get to the Overgrowth, the party can follow the smell of jasmine through the northernmost chamber of the Shallows. But if they ever smell lavender — RUN.

What will the characters encounter that makes them realize the failing Lure is a problem that needs addressing? What will they accomplish that shows them they’re capable of exploring further in? What about the community will coax them into returning — and what competition will light a fire in their veins? And most importantly, what culinary experience will change their view on beast-feasting forever?

#### Act 1

- The Inciting Incident is to enter the Plover Caves in order to track down the Ghost Scorpion Venom that Carat has asked about. This leads the party to discover the full extent of adventure in the caves, and may cause them to ask more about the Lure and its failing. If they return to Elmore with the Venom, then Carat will outright ask them to investigate the Lure so that the town may be safe in the long term, as the Venom barrier will only last for so long. Hopefully either the mysteries of the processed foods introduced in Stewpot, a rivalry with the Pickled Claw, or a draw from a character backstory will encourage them to explore deeper.

#### Act 2

- The basic design is to have regions modeled after each section of the food pyramid (inspired by A Crown of Candy), that are discovered as the players get deeper and deeper into the caves - in order of the inverted food pyramid. Stewpot is a melting pot location and the largest settlement, akin to a small New York City. From there, they'll encounter Verdancia, Grainspire, Berrywick, Carnivale, Dairydeep, and finally Bathyslard (the domain of The Refiner).

#### Act 3

- The players face off with the Refiner, and discover that the Lure is present here in the depth of Plover Caves, but its signal is being blocked by all of the fat and processed crap that the Refiner is pumping out.

#### Leveling Plan

- Level 2: At the end of the Act 1, once they've returned to Elmore with the Ghost Scorpion Venom and receive the Crumb-Crust Key, the party levels up.
- Level 3: After completing 1-02 (all of the areas around Verdancia, or upon arriving at Berrywick), the players level up.
- Level 4: After completing 1-03 (all of the areas around Berrywick, or upon arriving at Grainspire), the players level up.
- Level 5: After completing 1-04 (all of the areas around Grainspire, or upon arriving at Carnivale), the players level up.
- Level 6: After completing 1-05 (all of the areas around Carnivale, or upon arriving at Dairydeep), the players level up.
- Level 7: After completing 1-06 (all of the areas around Dairydeep), the players level up. The game will end with the players at Level 7 (Tier 3) during Act 3.

### Factions and NPCs

- **The Refiner (BBEG)**. An ancient force that seeks to halt the natural cycle of life, death, and renewal by locking food (and thus culture) into sterile permanence. It whispers that nothing should ever rot, spoil, or change — processing as false immortality. Its corruption appears differently in each region of the food caves.
>“Food is flawed. Nature is wasteful. I strip away imperfection, leaving only purity. One taste, forever.”

- **The Pickled Claw**. A loose guild of scavengers, hunters, and “preservationists” who make their living harvesting dangerous cave-creature parts and storing them in brine jars for trade. They carry belts full of clinking jars, glowing faintly from whatever venom or ichor sloshes inside. Their campfires always smell sour.
	- **Reputation**: Respected for their daring, distrusted for their ethics (they’ll happily destabilize a food chain if it makes them profit).

- **Krin Brinejaw** (he/him). Scarred leader of the Pickled Claw, and is a shrimp-like crustacean. Always chewing pickled stems, and speaks with a dry rasp. He is very utilitarian in his approach to things, and has no problem hurting people if necessary.
- **Chella** (she/her). A large blue lobster-like traveler originally from a place she calls "Wet Texas" (but couldn't point to on a map if asked). Chella loves pickled foods, enthusiastically joined the guild upon her discovery of it, and has risen to a respected position over the years. She is not an evil person, and could be negotiated with (especially if offered new and interesting pickles!).
- **Tallow** (she/her). Nervous record-keeper of the Pickled Claw, with a red crab-like appearance. Good with ledgers and jars but afraid of actual beasts.

### Locations

- **Elmore**. 
- **Plover Cave**. 

- **Shallows**. The first layer of the caves that spans from the entrance to the near-suicidal drop into The Stew Sea.
	- **Stewpot** (City, Orange). Stone terraces and steaming cisterns tucked against the cavern wall, always smelling of broth. Lanterns glow over communal cookfires where everyone shares meals. This is a true melting pot of natives, people from Elmore, the five food group cities, and the wilds of the caves.
	- **Brilliance**. A geodesic dome that shines so brightly it mimics the sunlight from the outside world. Some veteran explorers practice meditation and morning rituals in this dome, often asking one another, “Will you be at Brilliance today?”
	- **Overgrowth**. A glassy hollow where pale scorpions clatter across stone. Their circular nests flatten grasses into strange patterns, and their venom glows faint red. Combat with ghost scorpions to harvest venom happens here.
	- **Portobellows**. A damp fungal forest stretches into the dark, its spongy floor slick with rot and heat. Towering mushroom trunks rise into a canopy that drips glowing dew. The air tastes faintly of smoke and garlic, and the rhythmic puff of Hotspore clouds makes your tongue tingle.
	- **Crumb-Crust Ruins, Old Broth Falls and The Stew Sea**. A labyrinth of decaying breadstone towers slumps beneath the cavern ceiling, their crusts dark with broth. Rising water glugs between cracks, thick as gravy, creeping toward the ledges that overlook the roaring Old Broth Falls.
- **Twilight**. The second layer of the caves that ends at Reflection of the Stars, and serves as the limit of regular explorations.
	- **Verdancia** (Village, Green). A vast subterranean garden where enormous root-veins and leafy canopies twist into cultivated terraces. The air smells of herbs and soil. Many plants have semi-magical properties.
	- **Rosemary's Pass**.
	- **Chicory Grove**.
	- **Mallow Marsh**.
	- **Berrywick** (Village, Blue). A glittering cavern dripping with crystalline sugar formations and glowing fruiting vines. The air is sticky-sweet, but rot spreads quickly if left unchecked.
	- **Rock Candy Ravine**. Walls of crystalline rock candy that resonates in response to sound. Location of the rumored magical instrument (from Ambrose's backstory).
	- **Reflection of the Stars**. Plover Caves’ primary lake. It’s fed by an underground spring and sits beneath a ceiling dotted with bioluminescent morsels, such as the glowing mantis and the brightclaw scorpion. The aquatic creatures who call this place home range from small almond guppies to medium-sized jellyfish to the dreaded ironshark and the massive angler squid, whose many eyes are considered a delicacy.
	- **Grainspire** (Village, Yellow). A soaring cavern where stalactites and terraces resemble stacked loaves and towers of bread. Wheat-like plants sway in the drafts, and windmills carved into the stone grind cave-grain into flour.
	- **Wet Noodle Nook**.
- **Abyss**. The third layer of the caves is split between an underwater system of caves fed from Reflection of the Stars and the Catacombs.
	- **The Abisque**. A network of underwater caverns that are home to diverse and fascinating creatures, due to being fed by Reflection of the Stars. It feels a bit alien, as if astral creatures are swimming just below the stars.
	- **Barbacove**. The entrance point from the Abisque into Carnivale.
	- **Carnivale** (Village, Red). Jagged cliffs where hunting camps cling to ledges and rivers teem with blind cavefish. Echoes of hunts and feasts fill the air. Some warriors wear bone masks carved from their quarry.
	- **Slowroast Springs**. 
	- **Kabob Point**. 
	- **The Catacombs**. The area that separates Carnivale from Dairydeep, and the deepest point of the third layer of the cavern, thus named because the ground is covered in so many layers of bones, one cannot step without breaking a few and drawing attention to themself. Some of Plover Caves’ residents say the most horrifying beasts bring their prey to the Catacombs for consumption, making it a hotbed of dangerous creatures. Passing through the Catacombs successfully is the only way to explore deeper than the Abyss.
	- **Dairydeep** (Village). Cool, dripping caverns with natural cisterns and stone shelves stacked with aging cheeses. Mossy cows and shaggy goats graze fungal pastures under phosphorescent lichen.
- **Hadral**. The deepest point in the cave system, and home to dangerous, mythical, and gargantuan beasts.
	- **Sizzling Hollow**. 
	- **Bathyslard**. Here, natural variety is crushed out under endless weight, and everything is smothered beneath waxy fat, refined sugar-glass, and rubbery emulsions. Rivers of golden syrup run beside congealed slabs of processed cheese, while bubbling vats of oil preserve whole beasts intact, their eyes staring through translucent layers of grease. The air is stifling and tasteless, thick with a plastic tang.

#### Barry's (Restaurant)
- The sign outside simply reads BARRY’S, painted in deep red on a circular metal plate. The letters are clean, sharp, and unweathered no matter how damp or hot the cave air.
- Inside, the walls gleam like brushed tin and the air smells warm—something cooking, something comforting—but never the same. A row of stone-and-steel booths stretches along one side, each cushioned with soft red leather that squeaks faintly when you sit. Lanterns hang from chains above, their glass tinted amber, casting everything in the warm color of honeyed ale. Somewhere, unseen, you hear the steady hiss of cooking and the scrape of a spatula on an iron surface. The only other door in the building is behind the counter and marked "STAFF ONLY" in large letters.
- Then there’s Barry. Always Barry. Sometimes stocky and round-cheeked, sometimes tall and willowy, sometimes bearded, sometimes not—but seemingly the same person. Same smile, same calm voice that cuts through the kitchen’s rhythm. They greet you like old friends and hand you a slate etched with a short, smudged menu written in chalky white grease.
- These restaurants have a very "otherworldly diner" vibe, and are the only restaurant chain in the Plover Caves.
- **Pantry Door**
	- Behind the counter, there’s always one door marked STAFF ONLY. Always locked, with the same brass handle shaped like a fork.
	- If someone manages to open it (or catches Barry walking through), it reveals another Barry’s kitchen—sometimes hundreds of miles away. The door only works when Barry wills it. Perfect for your fast-travel system, or an eventual side-quest mystery.
- **Menu** (Identical Everywhere, Never the Same Twice)
	- Root Roast – Charred root vegetables slathered in thick, peppery gravy. Always tastes exactly like whatever meal you wish your parents had made more often.
	- Cave Cobbler – Fruitless, meatless, sometimes both; sweet-savory and steaming. The crust always forms your favorite shape.
	- Night Hash – Shredded tubers and some sort of meat (no one’s sure what sort), fried until the edges are the color of burnt sugar. Served with a drizzle of “Barry Sauce”—spicy, tangy, and faintly electric.
	- Luminous Pancakes – Stack of three, faintly glowing from bioluminescent syrup harvested “locally.” Customers who lick the plate report mild euphoria or sudden déjà vu.
	- The Traveler’s Plate – Only available if you order without looking at the menu. Comes out different every time, but always with the same garnish: one sprig of green herb that hums faintly when touched.

### GM Notes

##### Standard Ingredients List
The 23 standardized ingredients below are designed to be general enough to be scavenged from any adversary in Daggerheart. All flavor combinations are unique, and names are intended to be just silly enough to fit in the vibe of the campaign frame.
- Sulfurous Shells (Eggs) — Salty + Savory + Weird
- Muscle Morsels (Meat) — Savory + Savory + Savory
- Ichorous Innards (Organs) — Bitter + Bitter + Sour
- Brothy Bones (Bones & Marrow) — Salty + Savory
- Crunchy Carapace (Chitin & Scales) — Salty + Bitter + Weird
- Flappy Fillets (Wings) — Sweet + Savory
- Hardy Hide — Salty + Salty + Bitter
- Rotted Remains — Bitter + Sour + Weird
- Gnarly Greens (Leafy Greens) — Bitter + Bitter
- Rooty Rations (Roots & Tubers) — Sweet + Bitter + Savory
- Gilded Grains (Starches & Grains) — Sweet + Sour + Savory 
- Aromatic Alliums (Onions, Garlic, Leeks) — Sweet + Savory + Weird
- Fragrant Fruits (Berries, Drupes, Pomes) — Sweet + Sweet + Sour
- Funky Fungi (Fungal Caps) — Sour + Savory + Weird
- Nutty Nibs (Seeds & Nuts) — Salty + Bitter + Savory
- Candy Crystals (Crystallized Essence, Rocks, etc.) — Sweet + Salty
- Gooey Globs (Gelatinous Essence) — Weird + Weird
- Luminous Lactose (Milk from Plants, Insects, etc.) — Sweet + Salty + Savory
- Magical Membranes (Elemental Residue) — Bitter + Sour + Weird
- Sweet Secretions (Honey, etc.) — Sweet + Sweet + Weird
- Bloody Broth — Bitter + Savory + Weird
- Oozing Oil — Savory + Weird
- Ectoplasmic Essence — Salty + Weird
- Salty Spoils (Kelp, Dried Fish Flakes, Cave-Coral) — Salty + Savory + Weird

##### Special Ingredient Properties

- **Fiery/Spicy**: If your flavor dice match on results of 8 or higher, you can’t clear Stress using this dish.
- **Frosty/Cooling**: If your flavor dice match on results of 4 or lower, you can clear double HP using this dish.
- **Acidic**: For any matched set including dice of different sizes (d4, d8, d12, etc.), halve the Meal Rating contribution.
- **Shocking**: For any matches of three dice, double the Meal Rating contribution.

##### Adversary Ingredients

###### Core Book – Tier One
- Acid Burrower (Solo, HP 8) → Magical Membranes (Acidic) ×2, Muscle Morsels
- Bear (Bruiser, HP 6) → Muscle Morsels, Hardy Hide
- Cave Ogre (Solo, HP 8) → Ichorous Innards ×2, Candy Crystals
- Construct (Solo, HP 9) → Candy Crystals, Oozing Oil ×2
- Deeproot Defender (Bruiser, HP 6) → Gnarly Greens, Rooty Rations
- Dire Wolf (Skulk, HP 5) → Muscle Morsels, Hardy Hide
- Giant Mosquitoes (Horde, HP 9) → Flappy Fillets, Crunchy Carapace, Bloody Broth
- Giant Rat (Minion, HP 1 each) → Muscle Morsels (per group)
- Giant Scorpion (Bruiser, HP 7) → Crunchy Carapace, Muscle Morsels
- Glass Snake (Standard, HP 5) → Crunchy Carapace ×2
- Minor Chaos Elemental (Solo, HP 7) → Ectoplasmic Essence, Gooey Globs
- Minor Fire Elemental (Solo, HP 9) → Ectoplasmic Essence, Magical Membranes (Fiery) ×2
- Minor Demon (Solo, HP 8) → Ichorous Innards, Magical Membranes (Fiery) ×2
- Minor Treant (Minion, HP 1 each) → Gnarly Greens (per group)
- Green Ooze (Skulk, HP 5) → Gooey Globs, Magical Membranes (Acidic)
- Tiny Green Ooze (Skulk, HP 2) → Gooey Globs
- Red Ooze (Skulk, HP 5) → Gooey Globs, Magical Membranes (Fiery)
- Tiny Red Ooze (Skulk, HP 2) → Gooey Globs
- Skeleton Warrior (Standard, HP 3) → Brothy Bones
- Tangle Bramble Swarm (Horde, HP 9) → Gnarly Greens ×2, Rooty Rations

- Chaos Skull (Ranged, HP 5) → Ectoplasmic Essence, Brothy Bones
- Demonic Hound Pack (Horde, HP 9) → Muscle Morsels ×2, Rotted Remains
- Electric Eels (Horde, HP 10) → Muscle Morsels, Magical Membranes (Shocking), Salty Spoils
- Giant Eagle (Skulk, HP 4) → Flappy Fillets, Sulfurous Shells
- Juvenile Flickerfly (Solo, HP 10) → Flappy Fillets, Crunchy Carapace, Sweet Secretions
- Shark (Bruiser, HP 6) → Muscle Morsels ×2
- Stonewraith (Skulk, HP 9) → Candy Crystals ×2, Muscle Morsels

###### Core Book – Tier Three
- Adult Flickerfly (Solo, HP 12) → Flappy Fillets, Crunchy Carapace, Sweet Secretions, Luminous Lactose
- Dire Bat (Skulk, HP 5) → Flappy Fillets ×2
- Dryad (Leader, HP 8) → Gnarly Greens ×2, Aromatic Alliums
- Elemental Spark (Minion, HP 1 each) → Magical Membranes (Shocking)
- Greater Earth Elemental (Bruiser, HP 10) → Candy Crystals ×2, Nutty Nibs
- Greater Water Elemental (Support, HP 5) → Magical Membranes (Frosty), Salty Spoils
- Huge Green Ooze (Skulk, HP 7) → Gooey Globs, Magical Membranes (Acidic)
- Hydra (Solo, HP 10) → Hardy Hide, Crunchy Carapace, Ichorous Innards
- Oak Treant (Bruiser, HP 7) → Gnarly Greens, Nutty Nibs
- Treant Sapling (Minion, HP 1 each) → Gnarly Greens
- Young Ice Dragon (Solo, HP 10) → Hardy Hide, Crunchy Carapace, Magical Membranes (Frosty)

##### Specific Creatures and Special Ingredients
- **Ghost Scorpion** (Ghost Scorpion Venom, aka Hot Sauce). A bright yellow scorpion with an even brighter red pepper-shaped stinging tail.
	- Use Giant Scorpion from CRB (Bruiser, HP 7) → Crunchy Carapace, Muscle Morsels
- **Salad Sentinel** (Ranchheart Emulsion). A hulking tangle of iceberg and romaine, its leafy body held together by snapping cucumber-vine sinew. Shards of golden crouton form a rough, gravel-like armor across its chest and fists. Cherry tomato “eyes” glow red from a face dripping with thick streams of ranch dressing, while shredded carrots and onions sprout like wiry hair from its head and shoulders. When it moves, it gives off a cool dairy tang mixed with the earthy scent of garden soil.
	- Use Deeproot Defender from CRB (Bruiser, HP 6) → Gnarly Greens, Rooty Rations
- **Chutney Chimera** (Prismatic Chutney). A three-headed beast (mango, mint, and chili) with drooling maws, each dripping a different colorful paste.
	- Use Chimera from Void 1.5 - lowered to Tier 2 (Tier 2, Bruiser, HP 9) → Magical Membranes (Fiery), Fragrant Fruits, Gnarly Greens
- **Pesto Peryton**. A winged stag with green, leafy feathers that reek of basil and garlic; oily residue drips from its antlers.
	- Use Giant Eagle from CRB (Skulk, HP 8) → Flappy Fillets, Sulfurous Shells
- **Salsa Salamander**. A fire-elemental lizard whose scales are flecked with diced red, green, and yellow — like peppers, onions, and tomatoes. It constantly dribbles spicy juices.
	- Custom
- **Worcester Wraith** (Worcester Essence). A ghostly figure that leaves behind streaks of dark, vinegar-and-molasses-smelling mist. Its voice rattles with fermented depth.
	- Use Whisper Wraith from Void 1.5 (Tier 3, Ranged, HP 6) → Ectoplasmic Essence ×2
- **Nutmeg Naga**. A subtly crimson-colored half-serpent creature adorned with an ornate necklace of earthy-colored seeds. Rattling its tails releases nutty-sweet powder.
	- Use Giant Glass Snake, upscaled to Tier 2 (from FCG Homebrew, Solo, HP 8) → Crunchy Carapace, Nutty Nibs ×2
- **Saffron Spider**. A large spider with a skull-like abdomen and a subtle golden glow. Silk threads glisten gold, infused with saffron essence.
	- Custom
- **Ginger Golem**. An animated anthropomorphic being with a soil-based body rooted (and held together) with spiced ginger root. Slight gingerbread-man features give it a sort of whimsy.
	- Use Stone Sentinel, upscaled to Tier 2 (from FCG Homebrew, Solo, HP 9) → Rooty Rations ×2, Candy Crystals
- **Caramelized Slime**. Sugar-hard shell around a gooey center.
	- Custom (built in FCG, Standard, HP 5) → Candy Crystals, Sweet Secretions
- **Butter Basilisk**. A large winged and crowned snake, with a barbed tail and tongue, and a strong venom. Its gaze curdles dairy into butter.
	- Custom
- **Truffle Troll**. A large and bumbling pig-like humanoid with red eyes. Fungal growths on its back are black truffles.
	- Use Mountain Troll from Void 1.5 (Tier 1, Solo, HP 8) → Funky Fungi ×2, Hardy Hide
- **Caviar Kraken**. Eggs glisten like black pearls.
	- Custom
- **Creamy Crab**. A large albino crab with spoon-shaped claws. Its shell smooth and porcelain white with faint golden swirls, with steam seeping gently from its joints.
	- Mub Crab (Minion) - homebrew
- **Wasabi Wyrmling**. Bright green draconic hatchlings with sinus-clearing venom.
	- Custom
- **Ale Elemental**. Frothing body, burps yeasty bubbles.
	- Custom
- **Aioli Abomination**. A pale, quivering ooze with swirling veins of emulsified oil; its surface sometimes crusts with flecks of garlic, paprika, or lemon. When agitated, it splits into multiples, each tasting slightly different.
	- Custom
- **Neapolitan Necromancer**. A towering, skeletal figure draped in robes that swirl like layered ice cream — pink strawberry stains that drip like blood, dark chocolate shadows, and pale vanilla bones. The air around it chills with a cloying sweetness, like a parlor turned graveyard. Its staff is a giant waffle cone cracked with dark magic. The Necromancer summons/houses three types of undead minions:
	- **Vanilla Zombies** (Radiant Husk): Pale, frosted corpses that buff allies with steadiness and grant resistance to necrotic.
	- **Chocolate Zombies** (Bitter Husk): Dark, cracked corpses that hit hard with shadowy fists and deal extra damage when the target is weakened.
	- **Strawberry Zombies** (Sweet Husk): Rosy, syrup-stained corpses that charm or distract enemies, luring them closer with a cloying sweetness.
- **Saucefiend, the Mother of All**. A flowing elemental, constantly shifting between velvety textures: cream-thick béchamel, glossy brown espagnole, golden velouté, tangy tomato, buttery hollandaise. Each form changes its color, smell, and temperament.
	- **Ingredient**: Mother’s Base Reduction — a neutral stock-like substance that can be coaxed into one of the mother sauces by cooking it.

#### Treasure

- All village shops: Common Loot
- For scattered treasures as needed throughout the caves, use the below guidance based on depth:
	- **Shallows**: Tier 1 Weapons or Armor. Common Loot and Consumables.
	- **Twilight**: Tier 1 or 2 Weapons or Armor. Uncommon Loot and Consumables.
	- **Abyss**: Tier 2 or 3 Weapons or Armor. Uncommon Loot. Uncommon or Rare Consumables.
	- **Hadral**: Tier 3 Weapons or Armor. Rare Loot and Consumables.
- Specific treasure for each PC:
	- **Ambrose**: Improved Rapier (T2), Meridian Cutlass (T3), Tyris Soft Armor (T2)
	- **Flint**: Blunderbuss (T1), Ilmari's Rifle (T3), Harrowbone Armor (T2)
	- **Heart**: Improved Returning Blade (T2), Advanced Returning Blade (T3), Runetan Floating Armor
	- A set of Dragonscale Armor (T3) is found in Sizzling Hollow - the players can decide between them who gets it.

#### Travel and Randomness

- Any time the players are traveling from one place to another, it's important for a roll to happen to establish initial stakes at the new location and to open up potential for random combat to drain resources (forcing use of the Beast Feast mechanic). A group Instinct check (with the Difficulty based on the current area):
	- A success means that the players find wherever they're looking for without further issue.
	- A critical success means they find some additional loot or consumable (roll on the tables on pages 129 to 133). Hope and fear work as usual, ramping up or down current the situation.
	- A failure means that a random encounter may happen, based on the table below.

| d20   | Random Encounter                                                 |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1-2   | 1 Acid Burrower and 1 Cave Ogre                                  |
| 3-4   | 1 Stonewraith                                                    |
| 5-6   | `dice:1d4` Dire Wolves                                           |
| 7-8   | `dice: 1d4` Bears                                                |
| 9-10  | Players get lost and lose `dice:1d6` ingredients in the process. |
| 11-14 | The Pickled Claw makes an appearance.                            |
| 15-20 | Seemingly nothing happens - tick up a long term countdown.       |


#### Misc. Thoughts/Ideas

- If needed, I think Elmore is located just north of Cliffscrape (in the Lhazaar Principalities), on the coast of Cliff's End, between the southern Hoarfrost Mountains (containing the Plover Caves) and the southern Whitepine Forest (containing Plover Woods). This puts it far enough from civilization to make sense.
- Use Portal Seeds from the CRB as a fast travel method? (may not be needed now that we have Barry's)
- Hotspore (aka “Red Choir”) - a drug that can be seeded throughout the cave and might be alluring for those with a history (Ambrose). Sourced from a glowing crimson mushroom known as the Smoldercap, which sprouts in clusters often near volcanic vents. When cut, its gills ooze a thick, smoky sap that burns faintly on the tongue. Within moments, a deep warmth spreads through the body. Colors saturate, shadows pulse to unseen rhythms, and sound takes on impossible texture — every echo becomes a harmony. Users claim they can “hear the world breathing” and sometimes join in, humming in strange unison with the cavern’s resonance. Prolonged use stains the fingertips and tongue a rusty red, and eventually dulls one’s true hearing, leaving only phantom music behind. Heavy users are said to fall under the influence of the “Red Choir,” a hallucinatory chorus that never stops singing.
- "The Obelick" is the only unused location name that I liked. Keep in mind possible ways in which this location could be used - such as if a player needs a particular item or information at the end of the game.
